title: Operational Analysis in Practice: Common Case Types
summary: How operational analysis is applied to the cases FIUs see most often, from fraud and corruption to drug trafficking, tax crime and terrorist financing, and the financial indicators each tends to show.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How operational analysis is applied to the cases FIUs see most often, from fraud and corruption to drug trafficking, tax crime and terrorist financing, and the financial indicators each tends to show.
Learning Objectives: Recognise the financial footprint of the main predicate offences
Apply case-specific indicators to prioritise and develop analysis
Identify when a case needs specialist or multi-agency input
Syllabus: Fraud, corruption and politically exposed persons
Drug trafficking, organised crime and cash-intensive laundering
Tax crime, trade-based laundering and professional enablers
Intended Audience: Operational and strategic analysts in financial intelligence units
FIU heads of analysis, team leaders and staff managing intake, dissemination and international cooperation
Investigators and liaison officers who request, receive or rely on FIU intelligence
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial intelligence, investigation or AML/CFT work is helpful. No specialist analytical or data science background is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
Egmont Group (2013), Principles for Information Exchange Between Financial Intelligence Units
Egmont Group (2013, as updated), Operational Guidance for FIU Activities and the Exchange of Information
FATF (2013, as updated), Methodology for Assessing Technical Compliance with the FATF Recommendations and the Effectiveness of AML/CFT Systems
